guide.title: Inner Sunset, San Francisco: Irving Street, Grand View Park and the Mount Sutro trails
guide.intro: The Inner Sunset is the grid of numbered avenues south of Lincoln Way, and the wooded hills that rise behind it. Its two shopping streets cross at 9th Avenue and Irving Street, where Books on the Park, Ambiance, San Francisco Women Artists and Peasant Pies trade. Judah Street carries the Doelger Building of 1932, built for the firm that put tract housing across the Sunset District; 10th Avenue carries the Old Fire House of 1898; and the Sunset Branch Library opened on 18th Avenue in March 1918. The ground climbs to Grand View Park, whose summit is about 666 feet, and to the mosaic stairway on Moraga Street between 15th and 16th Avenues, 163 steps and 90 feet of it. Mount Sutro carries 61 acres held by UCSF and 20 more by San Francisco Recreation and Parks.

sections.heading: Irving Street, 9th Avenue and the Judah Street corner
sections.body:
The commercial ground is two streets meeting at 9th Avenue and Irving Street. Books on the Park is at 1231 9th Avenue and is known for new and used books; the Legacy Business Registry certified the business on 3 October 2016 under nomination number LBR-2015-16-022. Ambiance, women's clothing and accessories, is at 756 Irving Street, certified on 28 September 2020 under nomination number LBR-2019-20-025. Peasant Pies, hand-held savory pies and sweet pies, is at 1039 Irving Street, telephone (415) 731-1978, certified on 28 July 2025 under nomination number LBR-2024-25-043. San Francisco Women Artists keeps a gallery at 647 Irving Street at 8th Avenue, open 10:30am to 5:30pm Tuesday to Saturday, telephone (415) 566-8550, certified on 11 December 2023 under nomination number LBR-2023-24-017.

The Old Fire House at 1348 10th Avenue is San Francisco Landmark No. 29, designated in 1970: built in 1898 to a design by Charles Wilson, in a style San Francisco Planning records as Altered Shingle, with wide double doors and a tall hose drying tower. The Sunset Branch Library at 1301-1305 18th Avenue is San Francisco Landmark No. 239, designated in 2004; it was built in 1917 and opened on March 25, 1918. The Doelger Building at 320-326 Judah Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 265, designated in 2013, and merges Art Deco and Streamline Moderne in its stepped tower entrance, glass block windows and speedline canopy.

Bernard Zakheim painted the fresco cycle History of Medicine in California at UC Hall, 533 Parnassus Avenue, between 1936 and 1938, with his assistant Phyllis Wrightson and with part of the funding coming through the Works Progress Administration's Federal Art Project: 12 panels, 10 pictorial and 2 descriptive. The frescoes are San Francisco Landmark No. 289, designated in 2020. They were taken out of the building in 2021 and UC Hall was demolished.

sections.heading: The hills: Grand View Park, the tiled steps and Mount Sutro
sections.body:
Grand View Park is a San Francisco Recreation and Park property of 4.14 acres at 1730 15th Avenue, bounded by 14th and 15th Avenues and Noriega Street, open 5am to midnight. Its summit is about 666 feet (203 m) and is crowned with Monterey cypress trees. The hill is an outcrop of chert, which is part of the heterogeneous assemblage known as the Franciscan Formation, under a thin layer of sand, and it carries endangered Franciscan wallflower and dune tansy alongside bush lupin, beach strawberry, bush monkey flower and coyote bush. Residents call it Turtle Hill; the City's property name is Grand View Park.

The mosaic stairway climbs Moraga Street between 15th and 16th Avenues: 163 steps stretching 90 feet (27 m) high, faced with over 2,000 unique tiles from over 75,000 glass fragments, made by Aileen Barr and Colette Crutcher. Residents Jessie Audette and Alice Yee Xavier began the project in 2003, the steps were built in July and August 2005, and they opened August 27, 2005.

San Francisco Recreation and Parks records further property here: Golden Gate Heights Park, 6.96 acres at 2041 12th Avenue; Rocky Outcrop, 1.67 acres at 1800 14th Avenue; the 15th Avenue Steps, a mini park of 0.51 acres at 1060 Kirkham Street; J.P. Murphy Playground, 1.33 acres at 1960 9th Avenue; White Crane Springs Community Garden, 0.46 acres at 1620 7th Avenue; Tank Hill, 3.02 acres at 100 Twin Peaks Boulevard; and Grand View Open Space, 0.79 acres, for which the register gives no street address.

Mount Sutro is the high wooded ground. UCSF owns and manages 61 acres of Mount Sutro and San Francisco Recreation & Parks manages 20 acres on the east side; UCSF's own site calls it a vibrant, 61-acre open space reserve owned by UCSF as well as campus housing nestled amongst the trees. Sutro Stewards gives the trail network as over 5.5 miles; UCSF's own site gives more than 5 miles and a 900-foot elevation gain. The Interior Greenbelt, 21.37 acres, is the city property on the same slopes and the register gives it no street address either. UCSF's own site calls Parnassus Heights the original UCSF campus, made up of a tight network of buildings where faculty, staff, students and others are engaged in patient care, research and education activities, covering almost six blocks.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.body:
Steer by the addresses.

The shops and the shopping streets: Books on the Park, 1231 9th Avenue; Ambiance, 756 Irving Street; San Francisco Women Artists, 647 Irving Street at 8th Avenue; Peasant Pies, 1039 Irving Street. The Sunset Branch Library is at 1301-1305 18th Avenue, and gives 1305 18th Avenue as its mailing address and 415-355-2808 as its phone number. The Doelger Building is at 320-326 Judah Street and the Old Fire House at 1348 10th Avenue.

The high ground goes by street number as well. Grand View Park, 1730 15th Avenue, open 5am to midnight. The mosaic stairway, Moraga Street between 15th and 16th Avenues. Golden Gate Heights Park, 2041 12th Avenue. Rocky Outcrop, 1800 14th Avenue. The 15th Avenue Steps, 1060 Kirkham Street. J.P. Murphy Playground, 1960 9th Avenue. White Crane Springs Community Garden, 1620 7th Avenue. Tank Hill, 100 Twin Peaks Boulevard. For Grand View Open Space, the Interior Greenbelt, the Mount Sutro Open Space Reserve and the UCSF Parnassus Heights campus, no source states a street address, so none is given here.

faq.question: Which buildings here carry a register citation?
faq.answer: The Old Fire House at 1348 10th Avenue is San Francisco Landmark No. 29, designated in 1970. The Sunset Branch Library at 1301-1305 18th Avenue is San Francisco Landmark No. 239, designated in 2004. The Doelger Building at 320-326 Judah Street is San Francisco Landmark No. 265, designated in 2013. The Zakheim fresco cycle History of Medicine in California, painted at UC Hall between 1936 and 1938, is San Francisco Landmark No. 289, designated in 2020; the panels were taken out of the building in 2021 and UC Hall was demolished.

faq.question: When is the Sunset Branch Library open?
faq.answer: SFPL gives opening hours of 1pm to 5pm Sunday, 10am to 6pm Monday, 10am to 8pm Tuesday to Thursday, 1pm to 6pm Friday and 10am to 6pm Saturday. The phone number is 415-355-2808 and the mailing address is 1305 18th Avenue. The branch opened on March 25, 1918 and was the eighth branch in the San Francisco Public Library system; it cost $43,955 and was designed by architect G. Albert Lansburgh. It closed in 1992 for seismic retrofitting and to add a ramp and an elevator, and reopened in March 2007.

faq.question: What is at the top of the tiled steps?
faq.answer: The mosaic stairway runs up Moraga Street between 15th and 16th Avenues, 163 steps stretching 90 feet (27 m) high. Grand View Park is at 1730 15th Avenue, bounded by 14th and 15th Avenues and Noriega Street. The park is 4.14 acres, open 5am to midnight, with a summit of about 666 feet (203 m) crowned with Monterey cypress trees. The ground under it is an outcrop of chert, part of the heterogeneous assemblage known as the Franciscan Formation.

faq.question: How much of Mount Sutro can I walk?
faq.answer: Sutro Stewards gives the trail network as over 5.5 miles; UCSF's own site gives more than 5 miles and a 900-foot elevation gain. UCSF owns and manages 61 acres of Mount Sutro and San Francisco Recreation & Parks manages 20 acres on the east side, and the Interior Greenbelt adds a further 21.37 acres of city property on the same slopes. No source states opening hours or a street address for either, so none are given here.

faq.question: Which shops on Irving Street and 9th Avenue are on the Legacy Business Registry?
faq.answer: Books on the Park at 1231 9th Avenue, known for new and used books, certified on 3 October 2016 under nomination number LBR-2015-16-022. Ambiance at 756 Irving Street, women's clothing and accessories, certified on 28 September 2020 under nomination number LBR-2019-20-025, which records the business as established in 1983. San Francisco Women Artists at 647 Irving Street, certified on 11 December 2023 under nomination number LBR-2023-24-017, which records the organisation as established on 8 January 1925. Peasant Pies at 1039 Irving Street, hand-held savory pies and sweet pies, certified on 28 July 2025 under nomination number LBR-2024-25-043, which records the business as established in December 1993.

places.name: Old Fire House
places.summary: The fire house at 1348 10th Avenue, built in 1898 to a design by Charles Wilson. San Francisco Landmark No. 29, designated in 1970. San Francisco Planning records the style as Altered Shingle and the property type as government, and describes the building's wide double doors and tall hose drying tower.
places.history: It opened in 1898 and housed Chemical Engine No. 2. In 1900, Engine 22 was transferred here. After the 1906 earthquake the company spent 45 hours assisting in the evacuation of patients from Park Emergency Hospital on Stanyan Street, and the building also served as a food distribution center in the disaster's aftermath. It ceased operating in 1962. No source states its use today, so none is given here.

places.name: Sunset Branch Library
places.summary: The branch library at 1301-1305 18th Avenue, built in 1917. San Francisco Landmark No. 239, designated in 2004. SFPL gives opening hours of 1pm to 5pm Sunday, 10am to 6pm Monday, 10am to 8pm Tuesday to Thursday, 1pm to 6pm Friday and 10am to 6pm Saturday. The phone number is 415-355-2808 and the mailing address is 1305 18th Avenue.
places.history: Sunset Branch opened on March 25, 1918 and was the eighth branch in the San Francisco Public Library system. It cost $43,955 and was designed by architect G. Albert Lansburgh as a two story structure, Italianate in design, built of concrete frame and reinforced masonry; SFPL's own history calls it a Carnegie building. SF Planning records the style as Italian Renaissance; the library's own history calls the building Italianate. It closed in 1992 for seismic retrofitting and to add a ramp and an elevator. In September of 2005 it became the third branch to be renovated under the Branch Library Improvement Program, and the branch reopened in March 2007.

places.name: Doelger Building
places.summary: The commercial block at 320-326 Judah Street, built in 1932, which merges Art Deco and Streamline Moderne styles in its stepped tower entrance, glass block windows, and speedline canopy. San Francisco Landmark No. 265, designated in 2013.
places.history: The architect was Charles O. Clausen and the builder Henry Doelger Inc. The building was headquarters for Henry Doelger Builder Inc., and the firm built tract housing across the Sunset District; its tracts were affectionately called Doelgerville and Doelger City. SF Planning records Henry Doelger as the significant person associated with the building.

It carries endangered Franciscan wallflower and dune tansy, along with bush lupin, beach strawberry, bush monkey flower and coyote bush, and the summit is crowned with Monterey cypress trees. Residents call it Turtle Hill; the City's property name is Grand View Park.

places.name: 16th Avenue Tiled Steps
places.summary: A mosaic stairway on Moraga Street between 15th and 16th Avenues, made by Aileen Barr and Colette Crutcher: 163 steps stretching 90 feet (27 m) high, faced with over 2,000 unique tiles from over 75,000 glass fragments.
places.history: Residents Jessie Audette and Alice Yee Xavier began the project in 2003. The steps were built in July and August 2005 and opened August 27, 2005. The work was paid for by over 220 sponsored and named tiles and by the Mayor's Neighborhood Beautification Fund.

places.name: Mount Sutro Open Space Reserve
places.summary: The wooded reserve on Mount Sutro. UCSF owns and manages 61 acres of Mount Sutro and San Francisco Recreation & Parks manages 20 acres on the east side. Sutro Stewards gives the trail network as over 5.5 miles; UCSF's own site gives more than 5 miles and a 900-foot elevation gain. No source states a street address or opening hours, so none are given here.
places.history: UCSF's own site describes it as a vibrant, 61-acre open space reserve owned by UCSF as well as campus housing nestled amongst the trees.

places.name: UCSF Parnassus Heights
places.summary: The original UCSF campus located at Parnassus Heights is made up of a tight network of buildings where faculty, staff, students and others are engaged in patient care, research and education activities. Covering almost six blocks, the campus serves as headquarters for UCSF leaders. No source states a street address for the campus, so none is given here.
places.history: Adolph Sutro donated 13 acres at Parnassus Heights, at the base of the hill now called Mount Sutro, and the Affiliated Colleges buildings opened in the fall of 1898. UC Hospital followed in 1917 with 225 beds, the Clinics Building in 1934, the Langley Porter Clinic in 1942, the Herbert C. Moffitt Hospital in 1955, the Guy S. Millberry Union in 1958 and the Kalmanovitz Library in 1990.

places.name: Kogi Gogi
places.summary: Kogi Gogi is at 1358 9th Avenue, at Irving Street. Diners grill bulgogi, galbi and seafood at the table themselves, and the house all-you-can-eat special runs at $31.99 from Monday to Thursday. No source states its opening hours, so none are given here.

places.name: Um.ma
places.summary: Um.ma is at 1220 9th Avenue. Its tabletop grills are out on the back patio, which takes reservations, and Kurobuta pork belly and LA-style galbi are ordered by the pound and cooked at the table there under string lights. The indoor dining room serves Korean dishes that are not grilled at the table.
